topics.title: Getting started
topics.summary: Five tabs, one map. Here’s where everything lives and the fastest way to your first hunt.

blocks.p: OldGround puts old maps, LiDAR and satellite imagery on top of each other so you can find where people used to live and work, then keeps track of where you hunted and what you found.

list: **Map**: the one live map. Every “show on map” in the app brings you here, and it keeps your place when you switch tabs.
**Sites**: the fields, yards and parks you detect, each with its finds and visits.
**Finds**: every find, grouped by site, plus your other pins.
**Community**: finds and detecting videos shared by other detectorists.
**Old maps**: the scans you’ve imported and lined up.

blocks.p: Settings is the **cog** at the top of the Sites, Finds, Community and Old maps tabs.

steps: Open the **Map** tab and allow location so the blue dot shows where you are.
Look at the **LiDAR** (the map starts with LiDAR over satellite). Old house sites, roads and cellar holes often stand out as bumps and lines.
Import an old plat map or atlas page on the **Old maps** tab and line it up (see “Old maps”).
When you find a promising spot, outline it on the **Sites** tab with **+ New site**.
Get there, tap **Start visit**, and log finds with **+ Add pin**.

blocks.tip: Everything you make, from maps and sites to finds and paths, is stored on your phone and works without signal. Only posts you choose to share in the Community go online.

topics.title: The map
topics.summary: Satellite, topo, streets and bare-earth LiDAR, with your old map on top. Four ways to compare them: Overlay, Swipe, Split and Drive.

blocks.p: Along the top of the Map tab: **search**, the **view** you’re in, the **old map** on top, and **Layers**. Along the bottom: **Follow**, **+ Add pin**, and **Start visit** when you’re inside one of your sites.

list: **Overlay**: one layer over another, faded. Change how strong the top layer is with the **Strength** slider (tap the old map name at the top).
**Swipe**: drag the divider left and right to wipe between two layers.
**Split**: two maps, one above the other, moving together. Pan either one.
**Drive**: one full-screen map that follows you and turns with your heading. Good for scouting from the truck.

blocks.p: Tap the view name at the top to switch. Your choice is remembered.
Each view has small labels such as **LiDAR ▾** and **Satellite ▾**. Tap one to choose what shows there: Old map, LiDAR, Satellite, Topo or Streets.
LiDAR is a laser scan of the bare ground with the trees removed, from the US Geological Survey. Under **Layers** pick how it’s shaded:

list: **Stretched**: strong contrast; the best all-round look.
**Multi**: lit from several directions, so nothing hides in shadow.
**Move sun**: lit from one direction you choose. Turn the sun to bring out features running the other way.
**Slope**: steep ground is darker. Good for old roads, banks and foundations.

blocks.tip: Look for straight lines and right angles in the woods. Nature rarely makes them: old roads, fence lines, foundations and cellar holes do.

blocks.p: Federal, state, county and city land is shaded on the map. Tap a shaded area to see who manages it and what they generally allow. Always confirm the rules with the land manager before you dig. You can turn the shading off in Layers or Settings.

Tap the **magnifying glass** to search for a town, road or landmark, or type coordinates like **39.96, -82.99**. Tap **Follow** (the arrow, bottom right) to keep the map centered on you; move the map and it stops following.

Before you go, zoom to the area, open **Layers** and tap **Save this area for offline**. The satellite or topo you’re looking at, plus LiDAR, is stored on your phone. Very large areas are refused; zoom in a little and try again. Your old maps always work offline. Manage saved areas in **Settings › Offline areas**.

topics.title: Old maps
topics.summary: Import a scan of a plat map, county atlas or old topo and line it up with today’s map by matching a few landmarks. It then sits right on top, with your position on it.

steps: On the **Old maps** tab, tap **+ Add map**.
Choose **From Photos**, **From Files** (JPEG or PNG), or **Take a photo of a paper map**.
Give it a name, such as “1875 Licking County atlas”.
The app prepares it (cutting it into tiles so it stays sharp when you zoom), then opens the line-up screen.

blocks.tip: Scans up to about 220 megapixels work. Higher-resolution scans give a sharper overlay; photographs of paper maps work too, but hold the phone flat and square to the page.

blocks.p: The line-up screen shows the old map on top and today’s map below, each with a crosshair. You’ll mark the same spots on both. Each matching pair is an **anchor**.

steps: Pick a landmark that hasn’t moved: a road crossing, a church, a bridge, a creek crossing, a section corner.
Move the **old map** so its crosshair sits exactly on it.
Move **today’s map** so its crosshair sits on the same place. Search and the satellite/topo switch help here.
Tap **+ Anchor**.
Repeat across the whole sheet: near each corner and through the middle.
Tap **Done**. The app builds the overlay and opens it on the Map tab.

blocks.p: Two anchors are enough for a well-surveyed map. Old hand-drawn maps need many more, spread across the sheet, because their errors vary from place to place. With three or more, the map is stretched locally between anchors, like a rubber sheet, so each area lines up on its own.

list: **Green**: agrees with its neighbours.
**Yellow**: worth a second look.
**Red**: probably the wrong landmark, or the two crosshairs weren’t on the same spot.

blocks.p: Tap **List** to see each anchor’s error in feet or meters. Select one to **Move** or **Delete** it. On iPhone, **Mesh** shows the triangles between anchors; red ones are folded, which means two anchors cross over each other.

On the Map tab, tap the old map name at the top to switch maps or turn it off. In Overlay, the **Strength** slider in the same place fades it in and out. To fix anchors later, use **Line up** next to the map on the Old maps tab.

topics.title: Pins and finds
topics.summary: Mark finds, old houses, LiDAR features and permissions exactly where they are. Finds keep photos, depth, signal and detector, and the app can walk you back to any pin.

blocks.p: Tap **+ Add pin** on the Map tab, then either:

list: **Tap the spot** on the map where it is, or
tap **My spot** to drop it where you’re standing (your phone’s GPS position).

blocks.p: You can also **press and hold** anywhere on the map. It works on the old map too.

list: **Find**: something you dug.
**Old house**: a house or building site to hunt.
**LiDAR feature**: something you spotted in the LiDAR to check out.
**Permission**: a place you have, or want, permission to hunt.
**Other**: anything else.

blocks.p: A find can hold up to 4 photos, a type (coin, relic, button, jewelry, token), the metal, depth, the target ID number (VDI), the detector and its settings, a star rating and notes. Your detector is remembered for the next find, so you only type it once.

blocks.tip: Photograph the find before cleaning it, next to the hole, then again cleaned. The first photo shows on the map.

blocks.p: Tap any pin to open its card, then **Guide me**. A line runs from you to the pin, with the distance and direction at the bottom of the map. Tap **Stop** when you’re there.
From the card you can also **Edit** a pin, **Share** it, or **Post** a find to the Community.

topics.title: Sites and visits
topics.summary: Outline each field, yard or park you hunt. Finds inside belong to it automatically, and every trip is a visit with your time, your path and what you found.

steps: On the **Sites** tab, tap **+ New site**.
The map opens. Tap each corner of the field or yard.
Give it a name and choose the access: Permission, Public land, My property or Club hunt.
Tap **Save and explore**. That only saves it: plan sites at home and visit them later. If you happen to be standing inside the outline, a **Start visit** button is offered.

blocks.p: Any find you log inside the outline belongs to that site, including finds logged before you drew it.

Start a visit from the site’s page (**+ Start** on its Visits card) or, when you’re inside one of your sites, with **Start visit** at the bottom of the map. While a visit is on, a clock runs there and on a bar above the tabs. Tap **End** (or **End visit**) when you leave.
Each day you hunt a site is a visit: the time you spent, the finds you logged and, if you have it switched on, the path you walked.

blocks.tip: For a site marked **Permission**, the site’s page has a **Permission** card: get the owner’s permission signed on your phone, keep their contact details and a log of your calls, and send them a report of everything you’ve found. See “Permissions”.

blocks.h: Your path and the coverage map

blocks.p: Each visit records the path you walk. The site’s page shows every visit’s path over the outline: the newest bright, older ones fading, so you can see which parts you’ve worked and which you haven’t. Tap a visit to pick out that day’s path and finds, and **Open ›** for its own page.

Paths are approximate: a phone’s GPS is usually off by 10–25 ft, so treat them as “I worked around here,” not lane by lane. The app ignores the drift while you stand still or dig. It keeps recording with the screen off if you allow location **Always** (iPhone) or **Allow all the time** (Android). To stop recording paths, turn off **Settings › Record my path on visits**; visits still keep their time and finds.

Tap a site on the Sites tab to see its finds photo (take one picture of everything you’ve found there, laid out together), totals, the coverage map and every visit by day. A visit’s own page shows that day’s path and finds and lets you share it. Tap the coverage map to open the site on the main map. **Edit** renames it, changes access, redraws the outline or deletes it; deleting a site keeps its finds.

topics.title: Permissions
topics.summary: Get permission in writing: the landowner signs a simple slip on your phone and gets a PDF copy. Keep their number and a log of your calls, get warned before it runs out, and send them a report of your finds.

blocks.p: Every site whose access is **Permission** has a **Permission** card on its page.

steps: Open the site from the **Sites** tab and tap **Get it in writing**.

Fill in the landowner’s name (and phone or email if you like), your name, how long it’s good for, and the conditions you’ve agreed: fill every hole, call before coming, not during hunting season, and so on. Add anything else in your own words.
Tap **Hand the phone to…**. The owner reads the slip and signs with a finger, then taps **Sign**.
Tap **Send a copy** to text or email them the PDF. Send one to yourself too, as a backup.

blocks.p: The slip shows the property’s outline, its size and location, the dates, the conditions and the signature. It’s saved with the site on your phone and is never uploaded.

blocks.tip: This is a plain-language permission slip, not a contract. Laws on detecting and trespass vary by state, and the owner can withdraw permission at any time.

blocks.p: Choose 6 months, 1 year, or until the owner says otherwise. From 30 days before the end, the site’s card on the Sites tab says when it expires, and turns red once it has. Tap **Renew** to get a new slip signed.

list: **Call** and **Text** buttons use the number on the slip.
**Contact log**: tap **+ Log** after each call, text or chat to note what was said.
**Finds report**: tap **Send** for a PDF of everything you’ve found there, with photos. Sharing finds is the best way to keep a permission for years.

topics.title: Finds and pins
topics.summary: Every find in one place, grouped by site, with quick filters for silver, gold, coins and your best finds. Export everything as GPX.

blocks.p: The **Finds** tab has two parts:

list: **Finds**: every find, grouped by site, as photos. Filter by metal, coins only, or four stars and up.
**Other pins**: old houses, LiDAR features, permissions and other pins, nearest first, with distance and direction.

blocks.p: Tap any find or pin to see it on the map. The paths you walk are kept with their visits, on each site’s page.
Tap **Export** (or **Settings › Export pins and tracks**) for a GPX file with all your pins and paths. GPX opens in most GPS units, Google Earth and other mapping apps.

topics.title: Community
topics.summary: Share your best finds and favourite detecting videos, upvote and comment. Anyone can read it on the website; posting is in the app. Your locations are never shared.

blocks.p: The **Community** tab shows finds and videos from other detectorists. Sort by **Hot**, **New** or **Top**, and filter to coins, relics, buttons, jewelry, tokens or videos. Everything is also public at **oldgroundapp.com/community**.

steps: Tap **+ Post** (or **Settings › Join the community**).
Enter your email. We send a 6-digit code: no password to remember.
Enter the code, pick a name, and agree to the community rules.
Tap **+ Post** and choose **A find**, or tap **Post** on a find’s card on the map.
Pick one of your finds to fill in the photos and details, or add photos yourself.
Add a title and, if you like, the story and the state it came from.
Tap **Post**.

blocks.p: Choose **A video**, paste a YouTube or Facebook link and tap **Look it up**. The post shows the channel’s name and plays on YouTube or Facebook.

list: Your map locations are never shared. A post shows the state only if you pick one.
The hidden GPS data in photos is removed before they upload.
Your email is never shown to anyone.

blocks.p: Tap **•••** on any post or comment to **report** it or **block** the person. Reports are reviewed within a day. Delete your own posts and comments the same way, or your whole account in **Settings › Delete my community account**.

topics.title: Settings
topics.summary: Units, your detector, path recording, keeping the screen on, public land, offline areas and exporting.

blocks.p: Open Settings with the **cog** at the top of the Sites, Finds, Community or Old maps tab.

list: **Units**: feet or meters, for distances and depths.
**Your name**: as it appears on permission slips.
**Detector**: filled in on each new find. Include your program and sensitivity if you like.
**Record my path on visits**: draws where you’ve walked on each site’s map.
**Keep screen on**: while the map is showing.
**Public land**: shading on the map.
**Offline areas**: what’s saved for use without signal, and deleting it.
**Community**: sign in, sign out or delete your community account.
**Export pins and tracks**: a GPX file.

blocks.p: The app’s version number is at the bottom. Include it if you contact support.

topics.title: GPS and accuracy
topics.summary: What your phone’s GPS can and can’t do, and how to get the most accurate pins.

blocks.p: Phone GPS is usually accurate to about 16 feet (5 meters) under open sky, and less accurate under trees, near buildings or in deep valleys. That’s plenty to find your way back to a spot, but not to the exact hole.

list: For a precise pin, **tap the spot** on the satellite or LiDAR rather than using **My spot**.
Give the phone a minute outdoors after opening the app; the blue dot settles as it locks on.
Keep the phone in a chest pocket or on top of your pouch rather than in a back pocket.
Old maps are only as accurate as their anchors. More anchors, spread out, mean a closer fit.

topics.title: Questions
topics.summary: Subscriptions, offline use, backups and getting help.

blocks.p: $4.99 a month, billed by Apple or Google. Cancel anytime in your App Store or Google Play subscriptions.

Yes. Your old maps, sites, pins, finds and paths are on your phone. Save satellite, topo and LiDAR for an area before you go with **Layers › Save this area for offline**. The Community and place search need a connection.
On your phone. Deleting the app deletes it, so export a GPX file now and then as a backup. Only posts you share in the Community are stored online.

blocks.h: Is it legal to detect there?

blocks.p: OldGround shows public land and who manages it, but rules change and maps can be out of date. Always get permission and check the land manager’s rules before you dig.
Email **support@oldgroundapp.com** with your app version (bottom of Settings). We usually reply within a day.
